0.en: I. The Concept of the State

en: A multitude of human beings can call itself a state only if it is united for the common defense of the whole of its property.

It goes here really without saying, but it is necessary to be noted, that this union does not merely have the intention of defending itself, but that it, let the power and the success be whatever it will, defends itself through actual warding off.

For no one will be able to deny that Germany is united for its common defense according to laws and words; but we cannot here distinguish between laws and words on the one side and deed and actuality on the other, nor say that Germany indeed does not defend itself in deed and actuality, but yet according to laws and words defends itself in common.
For property and its defense through a state union are things that relate wholly and entirely to reality and whose ideality everything else, only not a state, has.
zh: 一群人只有为了共同保卫自己财产的整体而结合起来，才能自称为一个国家。
这一点其实不言自明，但有必要指出：这种结合并不只是有自卫的意图，而是——不管它的力量和成败如何——通过现实的抵御来保卫自己。
因为没有人能否认，德意志按照法律和言辞是为共同防御而结合起来的；但我们在这里不能把法律和言辞这一面同行动和现实性那一面区分开来，也不能说德意志虽然不在行动和现实性中、却毕竟按照法律和言辞共同地保卫自己。
因为财产以及通过国家结合对它的保卫，是完完全全涉及实在性的事情，而它们的观念性，是别的一切东西都有、唯独一个国家没有的。

en: Plans and theories lay claim to reality insofar as they are to be executable, but their value is the same whether they are in actuality or not; a theory of the state, by contrast, is called state and constitution only insofar as it is actual.

If Germany pretended to be a state and constitution, although the forms of the same are without life, its theory without actuality, then it would speak an untruth; but if it really promised common defense with words, then one would have to ascribe to it the weakness of age, which, although it can no longer, still has a willing, or dishonesty, which does not keep that which it has promised.
zh: 计划和理论之所以对实在性提出要求，是因为它们应当是可行的，但它们的价值是一样的，无论它们是否处在现实性之中；与此相反，关于国家的理论只有就它是现实的而言，才叫做国家和宪法。
如果德意志假装自己是一个国家和宪法，尽管它的形式没有生命、它的理论没有现实性，那它就是在说一句不真的话；但如果它真的用言辞许诺了共同防御，那就得把老年的衰弱归给它——虽然再也做不到了，却总还有一份意愿——或者把不诚实归给它，即不守住自己许诺过的东西。

en: For a multitude to form a state, it is necessary for it to form a common defense and state power.
The manner, however, in which the particular effects and sides of the union flowing from this are present, or the particular constitution, is indifferent for the fact that a multitude forms a power.

What belongs to this particular manner and way can in general be present in a most manifold manner, and in a determinate state a complete lawlessness and unevenness in this regard can even take place, and in the consideration we must separate the two from each other: that which is necessary for a multitude to be a state and a common power, and that which is only a particular modification of this power and belongs not in the sphere of the necessary, but for the concept in the sphere of the more or less better, for actuality however in the sphere of chance and arbitrariness.
zh: 一群人要构成一个国家，为此就必须构成一种共同的防卫和国家权力。
但是，由此产生出来的那些特殊效果和结合的各个方面以何种方式存在，或者说特殊的宪法是怎样的，对于一群人是否构成一种权力来说是无所谓的。
属于这种特殊方式方法的东西，一般可以以极其杂多的方式存在，而且在某个特定的国家里，在这一点上甚至可能出现完全的无规则和不均齐；我们在考察中必须把两者彼此分开：一群人要成为一个国家和一种共同的权力所必需的东西，和仅仅是这种权力的一种特殊变形、不属于必然性的领域，而是就概念说属于或多或少更好的领域、就现实性说属于偶然和任意的领域的东西。

en: This distinction has a very important side for the calm of states, the security of governments and the freedom of peoples.

For if the universal state power demands of the individual only that which is necessary for it, and restricts the arrangements that this necessary be rendered to it to that, then it can in the rest grant the living freedom and the own will of the citizens and leave them still a great room to play, just as the state power, which is concentrated in the government as a necessary center, is looked at all the less askance by the individuals who are in the periphery for that which it demands as necessary and whose indispensability for the whole everyone can see, and does not come into the danger that, if the necessary and the more arbitrary [is] subjected to the center of state power, with the same strictness as is demanded by the government, the citizens likewise confound the two with each other and, if they become equally impatient against the one as against the other, bring the state into danger from the side of its necessity.
zh: 这种区分对于国家的安宁、政府的安全和各民族的自由来说，有一个非常重要的方面。

因为如果普遍的国家权力向个人索取的只是对它来说必需的东西，并且把使这种必需的东西得到提供的那些安排限制在这一点上，那么它在其余方面就可以给予公民活生生的自由和自己的意志，还给他们留下很大的活动空间；同样，集中在政府这个必需的中心的那个国家权力，在处于外围的个人那里，就它作为必需的东西所要求的、并且每个人都看得出其对整体不可或缺的东西而言，就更加不会被侧目而视，也不会陷入这样的危险：当必需的东西和较为任意的东西都被置于国家权力的中心之下时，公民会以政府所要求的同等严格，把两者也混为一谈，而当他们对这一方和那一方变得同样不耐烦时，就会从必然性这一面使国家陷入危险。

en: To that part of the actuality of a state which belongs to chance, the manner and way in which the entire state power exists in a supreme point of union must be counted.

Whether that which holds power is one or several, whether this one or the several are born or elected to this majesty, is indifferent for the single necessary thing, that a multitude make up a state; just as indifferent as uniformity or non-uniformity of civil rights among the individuals subjected to the universal state power.

Of the inequality of nature, of talents and of the energy of the soul — which inequality brings forth an even more powerful difference than the inequality of civil relations — there is anyway no question.

That a state counts among its subjects serfs, citizens, free noblemen and princes who themselves again have subjects, and that the relations of these particular estates themselves exist again as particular political members not purely, but in infinite modifications, hinders a multitude just as little from forming a state power, as that the particular geographical members constitute provinces of different relations to internal state law.
zh: 属于一个国家现实性中归偶然所有的那一部分的，还必须算上全部国家权力以何种方式方法存在于一个最高的结合点中。
掌权者是一个还是几个，这一个或这几个是生来就具有这种威严还是被选举出来的，对于那唯一必需的事情——即一群人构成一个国家——来说都是无所谓的；同样无所谓的，是在那些服从普遍国家权力的个人中间，市民权利是均齐的还是不均齐的。
至于天性、才能和灵魂能量上的不平等——这种不平等造成的差别比市民关系的不平等还要更加强有力——本来就无从谈起。
一个国家在它的臣民中间有农奴、市民、自由的贵族和本身又拥有臣民的诸侯，而这些特殊等级的关系本身作为特殊的政治肢体又不是纯粹地、而是以无限多的变化形式存在——这丝毫不妨碍一群人构成一种国家权力，正如各特殊的地理肢体构成对内在国家法有各种不同关系的省份，也同样不妨碍这一点。

en: In regard to proper civil laws and the administration of justice, neither the equality of the laws and of legal procedure would make Europe into one state, any more than the equality of weights, measures and money, nor does their difference cancel the unity of a state.

If it did not already lie in the concept of the state that the closer determinations of the legal relations concerning the property of individuals against individuals do not touch it as state power, which has only to determine the relation of property to itself, then the example of almost all European states could teach us this, among which the most powerful of the true states have thoroughly non-uniform laws.

France had before the Revolution such a manifoldness of laws that, besides the Roman right which held in many provinces, in others Burgundian, Britannic etc. prevailed, and almost every province, indeed almost every city had a particular customary law, and a French writer said with truth that whoever travels through France changes the laws as often as the post horses.
zh: 就真正的市民法律和司法而言，法律和诉讼程序的相同既不会把欧洲变成一个单一的国家，正如重量、尺度和货币的相同也不会一样，而它们的差异也不会取消一个国家的统一。
如果这并不已经包含在国家的概念里——即个人对个人的财产方面的法权关系的更具体规定并不触及作为国家权力的国家，国家权力只需规定财产对它自身的关系——那么几乎所有欧洲国家的例子都能教给我们这一点，在这些国家里，那些最强大的真正的国家都有着完全不一致的法律。
法国在革命以前有如此杂多的法律，以致除了在许多省份有效的罗马法之外，在另一些省份通行的是勃艮第法、不列颠法等等，几乎每个省、甚至几乎每个城市都有自己特有的习惯法，于是一位法国作家真实地说道，谁要是穿越法国旅行，他换法律就像换驿马一样频繁。

en: No less does the circumstance lie outside the concept of the state, by which particular power or according to which relation of the share of the different estates or of the citizens in general the laws are given, likewise the character of the courts, whether it is, in the different instances of the administration of justice in relation to the members, an inherited one or one proceeding from the supreme power or one granted by the citizens according to their free confidence or by the courts themselves, what extent the district of a determinate court has and whether it has determined itself by chance, whether a common supreme instance is present for the whole state, etc.
zh: 同样处在国家概念之外的还有这样一种情况：法律是由哪一种特殊的权力、或按照各等级或一般国家公民参与份额的哪一种关系颁布的；还有法院的性质，即它在司法管理的不同审级中、就成员而言，是世袭的，还是从最高权力那里来的，还是由公民按照他们自由的信任、或由法院本身授予的；一个特定法院的管辖区有多大，它是否是偶然地确定下来的；是否为整个国家存在一个共同的最高的审级，等等。

en: Equally independent of the state is, and just as non-uniform can be, the form of administration in general, then the institutions of the magistrates, the rights of the cities and estates, etc. All these circumstances are only relatively important for the state, and for its true essence the form of their organization is indifferent.
zh: 一般行政的形式同样是独立于国家的，同样可能是不一致的，此外还有官员的设置、城市和等级的权利等等。所有这些情况对国家来说都只是相对重要的，而就国家真正的本质而言，它们组织的形式是无所谓的。

en: The inequality of the contributions of the different classes according to their material value, but even more the inequality of the ideal side, namely of the rights and duties herein and of their origin, is found in all European states.

Just as the inequality of the contributions to state expenditures arising from the inequality of wealth does not hinder the state at all, so that the newer states rather rest upon it, just as little does that inequality affect it according to which the different estates of the nobility, the clergy, the burgher and peasant estate contribute and have the ground in the difference of the estates, apart from everything that is called privilege, that they contribute in a different proportion, because the proportion can be determined not according to the essential side of that of which a part is given up, namely not according to the side of working, which cannot be calculated and is in itself unequal, but only according to the side of the product.
zh: 各阶级的捐税按其物质价值而论的不平等，而尤其是其观念方面的不平等，即在这方面权利和义务及其来源的不平等，在所有欧洲国家里都可以见到。
正如由财富不平等产生的国家开支分担的不平等丝毫也不妨碍国家，反倒新近的国家正建立在它之上，同样，下面这种不平等也不影响国家，即贵族、教士、市民等级和农民等级各按不同的方式分担，并且在等级的差异中——撇开一切叫作特权的东西——有其根据：它们按不同的比例分担，因为这个比例不能按照被交出的东西的本质方面、即不能按照劳作的方面来规定，劳作是无法计算的、自在地就是不平等的，而只能按照产品的方面来规定。

en: Other chance [matters]: whether the different geographical parts of a state are differently burdened, what transformations and subordinate systems the contributions pass through, whether on one and the same field a city has the land tax, a private man the ground rent, an abbey the tithe, the nobleman hunting rights, the commons the grazing right, etc., and the different estates and bodies of every kind form their own relations in regard to contributions — all such chances remain outside the concept of state power, which as center needs only the determinate quantity and is indifferent to the heterogeneous flowing together in regard to its origin; just as in general the whole relation of the contribution can lie outside it [sc. the state] and it can yet be very powerful, if either, as in the old feudal constitution, [the vassal] in emergencies through personal services at the same time provides for everything he needs in his service, which he renders to the state, and for the rest the state has in domains the source of its revenues — or, as can also be thought, that in the latter manner the expenditures could be met altogether, where the state would not even as money power, which it must be in newer times, be a center of contributions, but [that] which it receives as contribution, according to the actual relation of most contributions, stands on the same footing of particular right with others who in relation to the state are private persons.
zh: 另外一些偶然之事：一个国家不同的地理部分是否负担不同，捐税要经历哪些变化和从属的体制，是否在同一块土地上，一个城市有土地税、一个私人有地租、一座修道院有什一税、贵族有狩猎权、村社有放牧权等等，以及各种等级和团体在捐税方面各自形成自己的关系——所有这类偶然之事都留在国家权力的概念之外，国家权力作为中心只把一定的量当作必需的，而对这种不同类的东西的汇合、就其来源来说是漠不关心的；同样，捐税的整个关系一般也可以处在它[即国家]之外，而它仍然可以非常强大，如果要么像在旧的封建采邑制中那样，[封臣]在紧急情况下通过人身方面的给付同时为自己在为国家所作的服务中所需要的一切操心，而其余部分国家则在领地中有其收入的来源——要么，也可以设想，开支完全以最后那种方式来支付，这时国家甚至不作为货币力量（它在近代必须是这样一种力量）成为捐税的中心，而是它作为捐税所收取的东西，按照大多数捐税的本来关系，与那些在国家面前是私人的人处在同一种特殊权利的地位上。

en: In our times there may take place among the members an equally loose or even no connection in regard to morals, culture and language; and the identity of the same, this former cornerstone of the union of a people, is now to be counted among the chances whose constitution does not hinder a multitude from constituting a state power.

Rome or Athens and also every modern small state could not subsist if the many languages that are current in the Russian Empire were spoken within its compass, just as little if among its citizens the morals were as different as they are in that empire, or as they and the culture already are in every capital of a large country.

The difference of language and of dialects, the latter of which makes the separation at the same time even more irritated than complete unintelligibility, the difference of morals and of culture in the separated estates, which makes human beings recognizable almost only by the outer shape — such heterogeneous and at the same time the most powerful elements the spirit and art of state organizations is able to overcome and hold together in modern states, as in the grown-great Roman Empire the preponderant weight of power [did], so that inequality of culture and of morals become a necessary product as well as a necessary condition that the modern states subsist.
zh: 在我们的时代，各成员之间在风俗、教养和语言方面可能存在同样松散的、甚至根本没有的联系；而这些东西的同一性——过去是一个民族结合的基础支柱——现在要算作偶然之事，它们的状况并不妨碍一群人构成一种国家权力。
罗马或雅典、以及任何一个现代小国，如果俄罗斯帝国通行的许多语言在它的范围里被使用，就无法存在；同样，如果它的公民中间的风俗像在那个帝国里那样千差万别，或者像它们和教养在一个大国的每一座首都里已经那样千差万别，也无法存在。
语言和方言的差异——方言同时还会使分离比完全听不懂更加刺激——以及在各分离的等级中风俗和教养的差异——它几乎只让人凭外在形貌才能相互辨认——这样一些异质的、同时又是最强有力的因素，在现代国家中，国家组织的精神和艺术能够克服并把它保持在一起，正如在变得庞大的罗马帝国中占优势的权力重量所做的那样；以致教养和风俗的不平等成为现代国家得以存在的一个必然产物，同时也成为一个必然条件。

en: That in religion — in that wherein the innermost being of men expresses itself and wherein, even if all other outward and scattered things may be indifferent, they nevertheless recognize themselves as in a firm center and only through this would be able to have trust in one another over the inequality [and] changeableness of the remaining relations and conditions and to be sure of one another — that herein there is at least identity, has likewise been found dispensable in newer states.
zh: 至于在宗教里——在人最内在的存在于其中表达出来的那个东西里，即使其余一切外在而分散的事情尽可以无关紧要，人仍然认出自己处在某个牢固的中心里，并且只有借此才可能对余下各种关系和状况的不平等[和]可变性互相信赖、彼此有把握——，说这里至少有同一性，这一点在较新的国家里也同样被认定为可有可无。

en: Even in the frostier Europe, the unity [of] religion has otherwise always been the basic condition of a state.
People knew of nothing else at all, and without this first being-one they found no other being-one or trust possible.

At times this bond itself became so energetic that it several times suddenly turned peoples that were otherwise strangers to one another and in national enmity into one state, which not merely as a holy community of Christendom, nor as a coalition binding together its interests and for their sake its activity, but as a worldly power, as a state, at the same time conquered in the war over the Orient, as one people and army, the fatherland of its eternal and temporal life.
zh: 即使在更冷峻的欧洲，宗教的统一一向是一个国家的根本条件。
人们完全不知道还有别的什么，而且没有这个最初的合一，就觉得不可能有别的合一或信任。
有时这条纽带本身变得如此有力，竟一再把本来彼此陌生、处于民族敌对之中的各民族突然变成一个国家；这个国家不只是在基督教的圣洁共同体这个意义上，也不只是在把各方利益、并为这些利益而联结各方行动的联盟这个意义上，而是作为一个世俗权力、作为国家，在越过东方地区的战争中，作为一个民族和一支军队，同时征服了它永恒生命和现世生命的祖国。

en: As little as before and afterwards, in the separation into peoples, the sameness of religions hindered wars and bound them into one state, so little does in our times the unlikeness of religion tear a state apart.

State power has known how, as pure state right, to separate itself from religious power and its right and to maintain enough stability for itself and to arrange itself in such a way that it [the state] does not need the church, and she is again placed into the condition of separation from it that she had in her origin from the Roman state.
zh: 先前也好、后来也好，在分裂为各民族的过程中，诸宗教的相同都既不曾阻止战争、也不曾把各民族结合成一个国家；同样，在我们这个时代，宗教的不同也不会把一个国家撕开。
国家权力已经懂得，作为纯粹的国家法，把自己同宗教权力及其权利分开，为自己保持足够的持续存在，并把自己安排成这样：它[国家]不需要教会，而教会又重新被置于与它分离的状态，这是教会最初从罗马国家那里产生时就有的状态。

en: To be sure, according to the state theories that in our times have been set up partly by would-be philosophers and teachers of the rights of humanity, partly realized in monstrous political experiments, everything else — only the most important of all, language, culture, manners and religion, being excepted — that we have excluded from the necessary concept of state power is subjected to the immediate activity of the highest state power, and [indeed in such a way] that it is determined by it, that all these sides are drawn along by it down to their smallest threads.
zh: 固然，按照我们时代那些国家学说——它们一部分由自命为哲学家和人权说教者的人提出，一部分已在巨大的政治实验中付诸实现——，除了最要紧的东西，即语言、教养、习俗和宗教之外，其余一切被我们排除在必然的国家权力概念之外的东西，都被置于最高国家权力的直接作用之下，而且[是这样]：它由最高国家权力来规定，所有这些方面直到最细小的线头都被它拉扯过去。

en: That the highest state power must bear the supreme supervision over the mentioned sides of a people's inner relations and over their organizations determined by accident and old arbitrariness, that these must not hinder the main activity of the state, but that it has before all things to secure this for itself and for this purpose not to spare the subordinate systems of rights and privileges, is self-evident; but it is a great advantage of the old states of Europe that, while state power is secured for its needs and its course, it leaves the citizens' own activity a free scope in the details of the administration of justice, of administration and so on, partly with regard to the filling of the officials necessary in this, partly with regard to the conduct of current business and the handling of the laws and customs.
zh: 最高国家权力必须对一个民族内部关系中上述那些方面、以及对它们那些由偶然和旧日任意所规定的组织行使最高监督；这些方面和组织不得妨碍国家的主要活动，而最高国家权力首先必须为自己确保这一活动，并为此不必顾惜那些从属的权利和特权体系，这是不言而喻的；但欧洲旧国家有一个很大的优点：在国家权力为自己的需要和自己的运转有了保障之后，它给市民自己在司法、行政等等细节上的作为留出自由的活动空间，一方面是在这里所需官员的任用上，一方面是在日常事务的经办以及法律和习惯的运用上。

en: Given the size of present-day states, the reality of the ideal according to which every free man is to have a share in the deliberation and decision on general state affairs is utterly impossible.
State power must concentrate itself in one center both for execution, as government, and for deciding on these matters.

If this center is secure for itself through the reverence of peoples and is hallowed in its unchangeableness in the person of the monarch determined by a natural law and [through] birth, then a state power can without fear and jealousy freely leave to the subordinate systems and bodies a great part of the relations that arise in society and their preservation according to the laws, and every estate, city, village, community and so on can enjoy the freedom of itself doing and carrying out what lies within its district.
zh: 以现今这些国家的规模，要每个自由人都参与对普遍国家事务的商议和决定，这个理想的实在性是根本不可能的。
国家权力无论在作为政府的执行方面，还是在对此作出决议方面，都必须集中到一个中心。
如果这个中心凭各民族的敬畏而自身稳固，并且在那个按自然法则和[通过]出生确定的君主身上、以其不迁不易而成为神圣，那么国家权力就可以不畏惧、不猜忌，把社会中产生的大部分关系以及这些关系按法律的维持，自由地留给从属的体系和团体；而每个等级、城市、村庄、共同体等等都可以享受这样的自由：凡是在自己辖区里的事，都由自己去做、去执行。

en: As the laws on this matter gradually emerged immediately out of the customs themselves as hallowed tradition, so [the] legal constitution, the institutions of the lower jurisdiction, the rights of the citizens in this, the rights of the city administrations, the collection of the taxes, partly the general ones, partly those necessary for the needs of the cities themselves, and the lawful use of the latter — everything belonging here has come together out of its own impulse and has grown up for itself, and since it brought itself forth, it has also preserved itself.
zh: 正如这方面的法律是逐渐直接从习俗本身作为神圣的传统产生出来的，法律宪制、下级审判机构的设置、市民在这方面的权利、城市管理机构的权利、捐税的征收——既有普遍的捐税，也有城市自身需要所必需的捐税——以及后者的合法使用，凡属此列的一切都出于自身的冲动聚合起来、自行生长起来，而自从它把自己产生出来，它也就把自己保持下来。

en: The organization of the church institutions, so extensive, has just as little been made by the highest state power, and the whole estate maintains and replaces itself more or less within itself — the great sums that are annually spent on the poor in a large state, and the far-reaching institutions directed to this, which reach through all parts of a country, are not defrayed by taxes that the state would have to order, nor is the whole institution maintained and conducted at its command.

The mass of property and income that belongs here rests on foundations and gifts of individuals, just as the whole institution, its administration and activity, [is] without dependence on the highest state power; as the greater part of the inner social institutions has made itself through the free action of citizens for each determinate extent of need and maintains its duration and life with precisely this freedom, undisturbed by any jealousy or anxiety of the highest state power, only that the government partly protects it, partly restricts the luxuriant overgrowth of such a part, whereby it would suppress other necessary [parts].
zh: 教会机构这种如此繁复的组织同样不是由最高国家权力做成的，整个系统或多或少在自身内部维持自己、补充自己——每年在一个大的国家里为贫民花出的大笔款项，以及为此而设、范围广大、贯穿全国各地的机构，都不是靠国家要去安排的捐税来支付的，整个机构也不是靠它的命令来维持和运转的。
属于此列的大量财产和收入，靠的是个人的捐赠和施与，正如整个机构及其管理和运作[是]不依赖最高国家权力的；内部社会设施的大部分，是靠市民的自由行动针对每一种确定范围的需要自行形成的，并且靠着这种不受最高国家权力任何猜忌或不安干扰的自由，维持着自己的持续和生命，只不过政府一方面保护它，一方面限制这类部分过于茂盛的生长——因为那样它就会压制其他必要的[部分]。

en: In the new theories, however, which have in part been carried out, the basic prejudice is that a state is a machine with a single spring that imparts motion to all the rest of the infinite wheelwork; from the highest state power all institutions that the essence of a society brings with it are to proceed, be regulated, commanded, supervised, guided.
zh: 然而在这些新的、一部分已经付诸实行的理论里，根本的成见是：国家是一台只有一个发条的机器，由它把运动传给其余那整个无限的齿轮装置；而一切由社会本质带来的设施，都应当出自最高国家权力，由它来调节、命令、监督、引导。

en: The pedantic craving to determine every detail, the unfree jealousy of the own ordering and administering of an estate, corporation and so on, this ignoble fault-finding with every own doing of the citizens that would relate not to the state power but only to some general connection, has been dressed in the garb of principles of reason, according to which not a farthing of the common expenditure that is made for the poor in a country of 20, 30 millions [may be spent] without [its] having first been not [perhaps] permitted but commanded, controlled, inspected by the highest government.

In the care for education, the appointment of every village schoolmaster, the spending of every penny for a window pane of the village school as well as of the village council room, the appointment of every gate clerk and court bailiff, of every village judge, is to be an immediate emanation and effect of the highest government, and in the whole state every bite is to be led from the soil that produces it to the mouth in a line that has been examined, calculated, corrected and commanded by state and law and government.
zh: 那种要把一切细节都规定下来的迂阔癖好，那种对等级、团体等等自己安排和管理自己事务的不自由的猜忌，那种对市民一切自己作为——只要它不关涉国家权力、而只关涉某种普遍关联——的鄙吝挑剔，被披上了理性原则的外衣；按照这些原则，在一个两三千万人口的国家里为穷人花出的公共开支，连一个铜板也[不得支出]，除非它先经最高政府不是[也许]允许、而是命令、检查、察看过了。
在对教育的操心里，每个村校教师的任命，为村校以及村议事室的一块窗玻璃花出的每一个芬尼，每个门吏和法庭差役、每个村法官的任命，都应当是最高政府的直接流出和作用；在整个国家里，每一口食物都要从出产它的土地到嘴边，沿着一条由国家、法律和政府审查、计算、校正并命令的路线来走。

en: This is not the place to set out at length that the center as state power, the government, [must] leave to the freedom of the citizens [that] which is not necessary to it for its determination, to organize and preserve the power, [hence] for its external and internal security, and that nothing must be so holy to it as to let and protect the free doing of the citizens in such things, without all regard to utility; for this freedom is in itself holy.
zh: 这里不是详细展开的地方：作为国家权力的中心，即政府，应当把那些对它完成自己的规定——组织和维持权力，[因而]对它对外和对内的安全——并非必需的事情交给市民的自由，而且对它来说，没有什么比让市民在这类事情上自由作为并加以保护更神圣的了，完全不顾及用处；因为这种自由本身是神圣的。

en: But as for utility — if it is to be calculated what advantage the special bodies' own administering of their affairs, their administration of justice, their appointing to the offices that become necessary in this, and so on, brings —, then there are three kinds of calculation here: the one, which goes to the tangible thing, the money that the highest state power thereby gets into its hands, — the other to the understanding and the excellence with which in a machine everything proceeds according to uniform step, the cleverest calculation and the wisest ends, — the third, however, to the liveliness, the contented spirit and the free and self-respecting feeling of self-worth that springs from the participation of one's own will in general affairs, insofar as their branches are accidental for the highest state power.
zh: 至于用处——如果要计算：由那些特殊团体自己管理自己的事务、自己的司法、自己任命为此所需的官员等等，究竟带来什么好处——，那么这里有三种计算：一种着眼于摸得着的东西，即最高国家权力由此拿到手里的钱——另一种着眼于知性和那种卓越：在一台机器里，一切都按整齐划一的步调、按最聪明的计算和最明智的目的来进行——，第三种则着眼于那种活跃、满足的精神以及自由的、自重自敬的自我感受，它产生于自己的意志对普遍事务的参与，只要这些事务的分支对最高国家权力来说是偶然的。

en: In the first, the tangible one, the state whose principle is the universal machinery imagines itself without hesitation to be at an advantage over the one that leaves the detail for the most part to the rights and the own doing of its citizens.
But it is to be noted in general that that state, if it does not impose heavier taxes altogether, cannot possibly have the advantage.

For in taking over all branches of administration, of the administration of justice and so on, all the costs of these must at the same time fall upon it, which costs, if the whole is arranged according to a universal hierarchy, must likewise be covered by regular taxes, whereas the state that, [in the case of] what is [required] in these institutions, which bear only on the accidental and the single, such as the administration of justice, education costs, contributions to the support of the poor and so on, also leaves the costs to these single instances, which are interested in them, sees these costs defrayed without the form of taxes.
Whoever needs the judge and the attorney as well as an educator, or according to his own impulse considers the poor, here pays alone.

There is no tax present, no one pays for a court, an attorney, an educator, a clergyman that he does not need; just as, when [someone] is chosen by the members themselves for the lower offices of authority, of the court, of the administration of city [and] corporation affairs, [the one chosen] is paid by the honor that thereby befalls him, but must demand payment from the state that he should serve, because this inner honor is lacking here.

Both circumstances — even if, in relation to the first, more money should be spent by the people, which is not to be believed — bring about: the first the difference that no one gives money for something unnecessary to him, for a need of the state that is not general, the other a real saving for all, both that the people there feels treated with reason and according to necessity, here with trust and freedom — a circumstance that chiefly makes up the difference of the second and third kind of calculation.
zh: 在第一种、也就是摸得着的这种计算里，那个以普遍机械装置为原则的国家毫不迟疑地自以为占了便宜，胜过那种把细节大部分交给市民的权利和自己的行动的国家。
但一般说来应当注意：那个国家如果总体上不征收更重的捐税，就绝不可能享有这种好处。
因为一旦它接过行政、司法等等的所有分支，这些分支的一切费用也就同时落在它身上；如果整体是按一套普遍的层级制度安排的，这些费用同样必须靠定期的捐税来弥补；相反，那种国家对于这些只涉及偶然和个别之事的设施——如司法、教育费用、资助贫民的捐款等等——所需要的东西，也把费用留给与此有利害关系的各个个别方面，于是它看到这些费用不必以捐税的形式来开支。
谁需要法官和律师以及一位教育者，或者凭自己的冲动周济穷人，在这里就由他自己付钱。
这里不存在什么捐税，没有人会为他并不需要的法庭、律师、教育者、教士付钱；同样，如果有人被成员自己选去担任较低的官府职务，即法庭、城市[和]团体事务的管理，那么[被选中的人]凭由此得到的荣誉就已经得到了报酬，但他必须向那个他本该为其效力的国家要求报酬，因为在这里缺少这种内在的荣誉。
这两种情况——尽管就前一种情况来说，人民本该花出更多的钱，这是不可信的——造成：前一种造成这样的区别，即没有人会为他不需要的东西、为非普遍的国家需要花钱，后一种为所有人造成现实的节省，两者都造成：人民在那里感到自己被按理性、按必然性对待，在这里则感到自己被以信任和自由对待——这一点主要构成了第二种和第三种计算之间的区别。

en: The machinelike, eminently intelligent, and to noble ends dedicated hierarchy shows its citizens trust in nothing, and hence can expect none from them either; - it is sure of itself in no achievement whose command and execution it has not arranged, thus it banishes voluntary gifts and sacrifices, shows the subject the conviction of his lack of understanding and the contempt for his capacity to judge and do what would be conducive to his private welfare, as well as the belief in universal shamelessness; hence it can hope for no living action, no support from his self-feeling.
zh: 这种机械式的、极明智的、献给高贵目的的层级制度，在哪一点上都不向它的市民表示信任，因此也从他们那里指望不到任何信任；——它在任何一项它没有亲自安排其命令与执行的业绩上都没有把握，于是放逐了自愿的赠予和牺牲，向臣民显示出对他缺乏理解力的确信、对他判断和做那些有利于他私人福祉之事的能力的蔑视，以及对普遍无耻的相信；因此它不能指望任何活生生的行动，不能指望从他的自我感受中得到任何支持。

en: There lies in this a difference that is too great for it to be grasped by the statesman who brings into account only what is to be calculated in definite numbers, a difference that shows itself first of all in the prosperity, the well-being, the honesty and the contentment of the inhabitants of the one state as well as in the dullness, the eternal turning over of baseness into insolence, and the poverty of the other, [and] who in the greatest matters, where only the accidental side of the occurrence lies on the outside, precisely determines this contingency and makes it necessary.
zh: 这里有一种差别，它太大，不是那位只把能用确定数字算出来的东西算进去的政治家所能把握的；这种差别首先表现在一个国家的居民的富裕、安乐、正直和满足上，也表现在另一个国家的迟钝、卑劣与无耻之间永恒的翻转以及它的贫困上；而这位政治家在那些最重大的事情上——在那里，露在表面的只有事件的偶然一面——恰恰把这种偶然性确定下来，并使之成为必然。

en: The difference is infinite whether the state power arranges itself so that everything on which it can count is in its hands and that for that very reason it can count on nothing further, or whether, besides what is in its hands, it can also count on the free attachment, the self-feeling and the own striving of the people, - an almighty, invincible spirit that that hierarchy has driven out and that alone has its life where the supreme state power leaves as much as possible to the citizens' own management.

How in such a modern state, in which everything is regulated from the top down, nothing that has a universal side is left to the administration and execution of those parts of the people that are interested in it - as the French Republic has made itself -, a leathery, spiritless life will be produced, is, if this tone of the pedantry of ruling can remain, only to be learned in the future; but what life and what drought prevails in another, equally regulated state, in the Prussian, that strikes everyone who enters its first village or sees its complete lack of scientific and artistic genius or does not consider its strength according to the ephemeral energy to which a single genius has known how to force it up for a time.
zh: 这个差别是无限的：国家权力究竟把自己安排成这样，即凡是它能指望的东西都在它手里，而且正因如此它就不能再指望别的任何东西；还是说，在它手里的东西之外，它也能指望人民的自由依恋、自我感受和自己的努力——一种全能而不可战胜的精神，那种层级制度已经把它赶走，而它唯独在最高国家权力尽可能把事情留给市民自己操办的地方才有生命。

在这样一个一切都自上而下被规定好的现代国家里，凡是有普遍性一面的东西都不交给人民中那些与之有利害关系的部分的行政和执行——法国共和国就把自己造成了这样——，这会产生一种皮革般的、无精神的生活，而这一点，如果这种治人者的迂腐腔调还能保持下去，只有将来才能知道；但另一个同样被规定得井井有条的国家，即普鲁士，里面流行着怎样的生活和怎样的干枯，这一点每个踏进它的第一个村庄的人、每个看到它完全缺乏科学和艺术天才的人、每个不是按某个单个天才曾懂得在某一时期把它硬抬上去的那种短暂能量来衡量它的力量的人，都会注意到。

en: We therefore distinguish in a state not only the necessary, what must lie in the hand of the state power and be determined immediately by it, and what is indeed absolutely necessary in the social union of a people but accidental for the state power as such, but we also hold that people to be happy to which the state leaves much free hand in the more subordinate general activity, and also hold a state power to be infinitely strong that can be supported by the freer and unpedantized spirit of its people.
zh: 所以我们在一国之内不仅区分出必然的东西，即必须落在国家权力手中、必须由它直接规定的东西，以及那种在人民的结合中绝对必然、但对国家权力本身却是偶然的东西，而且还认为，国家在较为次要的普遍事务上给它留下许多自由空间的民族是幸福的，也认为一种能被它的人民更自由、更少迂腐的精神所支持的国家权力是无限强大的。

en: That therefore in Germany the unfree demand is not fulfilled, namely to know laws, administration of justice, imposition and collection of taxes etc., language, customs, education, religion regulated and governed from one center, but that instead the most disparate manifoldness prevails in this regard, this would not prevent Germany from constituting a state, if only it were organized as a state power ...
zh: 所以，在德意志，那个不自由的要求并没有得到满足——即让法律、司法、赋税的摊派和征收等等，还有语言、习俗、教养、宗教，都由一个中心来规定和治理——，而是在这些事情上存在着最不相干的杂多；这一点并不会妨碍德意志构成一个国家，只要它被组织成一种国家权力……

30.en: [II. History and Critique of the Constitution of the German Empire]
30.zh: [II. 德意志帝国宪法的历史与批判]

en: The propagation of this warlike talent itself proves that these hosts of armed men are not idle; for centuries no significant war is waged among the European powers in which German bravery did not win for itself, if not laurels, always honor, in which streams of German blood did not flow.
zh: 这种战争才能本身的繁衍就证明，这些武装的人群并非无所事事；几个世纪以来，欧洲列强之间没有打过一场重大的战争，在其中德意志的勇敢不曾为自己赢得——即使不是桂冠——也总是荣誉，在其中不曾流淌过成河的德意志人的血。

en: With the multitude of its inhabitants, the warlike talents of the same, the readiness of their lords to shed their blood, with its wealth in the dead as well as in the living requirements of war, no country is more defenseless, none more incapable of not being conquered, of only defending itself, than Germany.
Not even the attempts at defense, the mere striving, is either significant or honorable.
zh: 就它有众多的居民、这些居民有战争的才能、他们的领主乐于让他们流血而言，就它在战争的各种死的和活的需求上都富足而言，没有一个国家比德意志更无防卫，没有一个国家更无能于不被征服、只求自卫。
就连防御的尝试、单纯的奋力，也既不重要，也不光彩。

en: The military power consists, as is well known, of the military of the larger and smaller estates.

As for the latter, these armies, hosts, troop corps, or whatever one wants to call them, can usually be no more than police and parade soldiers, not warriors who know nothing higher than the glory of their army and service.

The military spirit that lifts the heart of every warrior of a great army at the word "our army", this pride in his estate and service, the soul of an army, cannot thrive in the town watch of an imperial city, in the bodyguard of an abbot.
The kind of respect that the sight of the uniform of great armies awakens for the still unknown individual who wears it cannot fall to the uniform of an imperial city.

"I have been 20, 30 years in this service" in the mouth of the most upright soldier of a small imperial estate carries quite a different feeling and effect with it than in the mouth of an officer of a great army, for the self-feeling of the man and the respect of others for him grows with the greatness of the whole to which he belongs; he takes part in the glory that centuries have heaped upon it.
zh: 众所周知，军事力量由较大和较小等级的军队组成。
至于后者，这些军团、军队、部队，或者人们想怎么称呼它们都行，通常不过是警察和阅兵式的士兵，而不是除了自己军队和服役的荣誉之外不知道更高东西的战士。
那种在听到“我们的军队”一词时使一支大军队里每个战士的心都振奋起来的军事精神，这种对自己等级和服役的骄傲，一支军队的灵魂，在一个帝国城市的城防队里、在一个修道院院长的卫队里，是长不起来的。
大军队的军服一出现，就会为穿它的那个还无人认识的个体唤起某种敬意，而一个帝国城市的军服却得不到这种敬意。
“我在这项服役里已经待了 20 年、30 年”，这句话在一个小小的帝国等级的最正直的士兵嘴里，所带出的感受和效果完全不同于在一支大军队的军官嘴里；因为这个人的自我感受和他人对他的敬重，是随着他所隶属的整体的伟大而增长的；他分享着几个世纪堆积在这个整体上的荣誉。

en: The insignificance of the isolated small military corps through their small number need not be increased still further by awkwardness and other unfavorable arrangements.

It must have very great disadvantages that on the outbreak of a war the smaller estates first recruit their soldiers, often only now appoint the officers, thus send unexercised people into the field, that one estate has to supply the drummer, another the drum, etc., that because of the multitude of estates that send contingents together, inequality in the weapons, the drill, etc., and unfamiliarity of the common soldiers with the officers takes place, that each estate actually has the right to provide for the provisioning itself, so that the greatest disorder in the service and a hindering overload of civilians and baggage prevail besides the unnecessary costs.

According to juridical theory, there belong to a detached picket of twenty men of different estates actually twenty separate provisioning commissaries, bakers, etc.; that the imperial register is a few hundred years old, thus no longer corresponds to the present relation of the size and power of the estates and therefore gives occasion for discontent, complaints and eternal arrears, that in it districts occur whose geographical location can no longer even be ascertained, and a hundred other circumstances are too well known not to be boring when one mentions them.
zh: 那些分散的小型军团因其人数少而微不足道，这种微不足道并不需要再靠笨拙和其他不利的制度安排来加重。
这必定有非常大的坏处：战争爆发时，较小的等级才去招募自己的士兵，往往到这时才任命军官，于是把没受过训练的人送上战场；一个等级要提供鼓手，另一个要提供鼓，等等；由于送来兵力的等级众多，武器、操练等等参差不齐，普通士兵与军官彼此不熟；每个等级其实都有权自己负责给养，于是在服役中流行着最大的混乱，除不必要的花费之外还有妨碍行动的平民和辎重超载。
按法理学说，一支由不同等级的二十人组成的派出哨队，其实该配二十个自己的给养委员、面包师等等；而帝国名册已是几百年前的，不再符合各等级现在的大小和实力关系，因此招致不满、抱怨和永远的欠缴；名册里还列有一些连地理位置都再也查不出来的地区；此外还有上百种别的情况，都太为人所熟知，一提起来就免不了叫人腻烦。

en: If now the insignificance of the military of the smaller estates disappears when they assemble and coalesce into an imperial army, then the disadvantages mentioned and countless others put the usefulness of this army in war below all the armies of the rest of Europe, the Turkish one itself not excepted, and the mere name of an imperial army otherwise had a peculiar misfortune.

Just as the name of other, even foreign armies awakens the thought of bravery and fearsomeness, so rather the name of the imperial army, uttered in a German company, brightened every face, awakened all witty moods according to estate and due measure, and everyone reached into the bag of his anecdotes about it in order to give something of the best.

And if the German nation is held to be serious and incapable of the comic, then one forgets the farces of the imperial wars, which are performed with all possible outward seriousness but a genuine inner ridiculousness.
zh: 如果说，较小等级的军队在它们集合起来、汇聚成一支帝国军队时，其微不足道也就消失了，那么上面提到的以及无数别的坏处，仍然把这支军队在战争中的可用性压到其余欧洲所有军队之下，连土耳其军队也不例外；而“帝国军队”这个名字本身，从前就带着一种特别的不幸。
正如别的、甚至是外国的军队的名字会唤起勇敢和可怖的念头，帝国军队这个名字在一群德意志人当中说出来，反而会照亮每一张脸，唤起一切与身份相称的诙谐情绪，人人都伸手到自己关于它的轶事袋子里，好拿出点什么来逗乐。
而如果人们认为德意志民族是严肃的、不会滑稽，那就是忘了历次帝国战争的那些闹剧——它们是以一切可能的外在严肃、却带着真正内在的可笑上演的。

en: While the organization of the imperial army with all its consequences has improved in nothing, the feeling of the misfortune brought about by it and of the shame of Germany has diminished the general addiction to mocking it, and only because in the last war much in regard to it, e.g. the provisioning, was handled contrary to right and constitution, have these troops been able to be of some use.
zh: 当帝国军队的组织连同它的一切后果丝毫没有改善的时候，对由它造成的灾祸和对德意志的耻辱的感受，却减少了人们普遍爱拿它开玩笑的瘾头；而只是因为在上一次战争中对它的一些事情——比如给养——作了违背法权和宪法的处理，这些部队才可能有点用处。

en: Still more disadvantageous than all these circumstances of the constitution of an imperial army is it that actually one is never brought together; and herein the dissolution of Germany into independent states shows itself most visibly.
zh: 比一支帝国军队的性质方面所有这些情况更加不利的是，实际上从来就凑不出一支帝国军队来；而德意志分解为各个独立的国家，最明显不过地就表现在这里。

en: According to the theory of the fundamental laws the imperial army could be a formidable army, but practice, this mighty principle of German public law, shows something entirely different.

If one sees only too often an enormous multitude of German soldiers in the field, it is understood that they are on their feet not as an imperial army for the defense of Germany, but for the mangling of its entrails.
What one calls the German constitution is not only unable to prevent such wars, but rather makes them rightful and lawful.
zh: 按基本法的理论，帝国军队本可以是一支令人生畏的军队，但实践——德意志国家法这一强大的原则——显示的却完全是另一回事。
如果人们太经常地在战场上看到大批德意志士兵，那就不言而喻，他们出动并不是作为帝国军队去保卫德意志，而是去撕咬它自己的内脏。
人们所称的德意志宪法，不仅不能防止这类战争，反而使它们合乎法权、合乎法律。

en: All the more insignificant, by contrast, is the German army when it is called up for the protection of Germany; for although the fivefold contingents of Brandenburg, Saxony, Hanover, Bavaria, Hesse by themselves already form armies and united would be a formidable army and would make the awkwardness of the smaller contingents united with them disappear, they depend on something altogether different from the laws of Germany, and their cooperation in its defence [is] just as unreliable and accidental as the cooperation of any foreign power.
zh: 德意志军队在奉命保卫德意志时，就更加微不足道了；因为勃兰登堡、萨克森、汉诺威、巴伐利亚、黑森这五份兵力各自已经构成军队，合在一起更是一支令人生畏的大军，本来还能让随之联合的那些较小兵力的笨拙消失不见，可它们依赖的却是完全另一套东西，而不是德意志的法律，于是它们对保卫德意志的参与[也]完全和任何一个外部强国的参与一样不可靠、一样出于偶然。

en: With the great contingents — the Austrian one not included among them, which the Emperor, as monarch of other kingdoms, is compelled, on account of the weakness and unreliability of the obligated army, to increase far beyond its estate obligations and to let Germany enjoy the exertions and the extent of his power elsewhere — the Empire can count neither on their lawful strength, nor on their being furnished at all, nor on this, that the estate which has likewise furnished its contingent does not, in the middle of the war and in the most dangerous moments, conclude for itself neutrality and peace treaties with the enemy of the Empire and abandon the fellow estates that are attacked to their own weakness and to the devastating superior power of the enemy.
zh: 对于那些大兵力——奥地利的兵力不算在内，皇帝作为其他一些王国的君主，由于这支有义务的军队既虚弱又不可靠，不得不把它扩充到远远超出它按等级所担的义务，并让德意志享用他在别处的力量的投入和规模——，帝国既不能指望它们达到法定的兵力，也不能指望它们真被派出来，更不能指望这一点：那个同样派出了自己兵力的等级，不会在战争中间、在最危险的关头自行与帝国的敌人订立中立条约和和约，把受到进攻的同等级伙伴丢给它们自己的虚弱和敌人毁灭性的优势去摆布。

en: Although the imperial-law right of the estates to conclude alliances with foreign powers and to make the choice between foreigners and Germany is restricted by the clause "insofar as such alliances do not contradict the duties toward Emperor and Empire", this clause has been made ambiguous by practice as a legal principle, or rather eliminated, and so not merely the deed but estate votes in the imperial diet can go as far as this, that their other connections do not permit them to take part in the furnishing of an imperial contingent and in the payment of the contributions to the war.
zh: 尽管各等级依帝国法律享有的权利——与外部列强缔结同盟、在外国与德意志之间作出选择——受到「只要这类同盟不违背对皇帝和帝国的义务」这一附款的限制，这条附款在实践中作为一条法律原则已经被弄得含混不清，或者干脆被取消了，于是不仅实际行动，连各等级在帝国议会上的表决也可以走到这一步：它们别的联系不允许它们参与派出一支帝国兵力，也不允许它们缴纳这场战争的摊款。

en: This withdrawal of the more considerable estates from participation in the common defence puts others into a state of helplessness which compels them likewise to withdraw from the need and the danger, but thereby also from their obligations toward the whole.

It would be altogether unnatural to demand that they rely on a protection and contribute to it which, as all the world knows, protects nothing and is legally and by right refused through the right to conclude alliances.

Under such circumstances it becomes necessary that the weaker ones place themselves under the protection of those powerful fellow estates which are friends with the enemy and thereby likewise diminish the common mass of the shared power; in which way then those powerful estates gain not only by sparing themselves their exertions, but also by procuring from the enemy advantages for their inaction, and finally, in that they at the same time weaken the common mass by the contribution of those whom they compel under their protection, they likewise draw benefit from these for the protection rendered.
zh: 那些较有分量的等级这样退出共同防御，就把另一些等级置于一种孤立无援的境地，使它们也不得不从危难中抽身，但这样一来，也就从它们对整体的义务中抽身了。
要求它们去信赖一种保护并为它出力，是完全不近情理的，因为这种保护举世周知什么都保护不了，而且凭着缔结同盟的权利，它在法律上和权利上都被拒绝了。
在这样的情况下，较弱的等级就不得不投到那些与敌人交好的强大同等级伙伴的保护之下，从而同样削减共同权力的总量；这样一来，那些强大的等级就不只是靠省下自己的投入而得利，还从敌人那里为自己的无所作为换取好处，最后，由于它们同时又把那些被它们逼到其保护之下的等级的那份摊款从总量中抽走，它们还从这些等级身上为所提供的保护捞到好处。

en: Even if several great contingents have really come together, the instability of their relations and the unreliability of their staying together disturb the common effectiveness.

Over these troop corps there is not the free disposal which is necessary for the secure execution of a plan of war, and the plan not only of a campaign but of individual operations requires for the deed not so much orders as negotiations.

Nor can it fail that the calculation arises whether the contingent of a single estate is used too much, others on the other hand spared and the equality of right violated, just as in other state relations there otherwise arose dispute over the first place of danger and discontent over the non-use.
zh: 就算现实地有好几支大兵力聚到了一起，它们各自关系的飘忽不定、它们待在一起的不可靠，也会扰乱共同的行动效力。
对这些部队不能作那种为可靠执行一个作战计划所必需的[自由]调度，而不论是一个战局的计划还是单个行动的计划，要变成行动，需要的与其说是命令，不如说是谈判。
而且免不了会出现这样的盘算：某个等级的兵力是不是用得太多，另一些反倒被爱惜，权利上的平等是不是受了损害——就像在别的国家关系里，从前也会为谁先冒危险而争执、为没被派上用场而不满一样。

en: The jealousy of the different corps, which regard themselves as different nations, the possibility that they withdraw in the most critical moments — all these circumstances make it necessary that an imperial army considerable even in number and military content can produce no proportionate effect at all.
zh: 各支队伍彼此猜忌，把自己看作互不相同的民族，加上它们有可能在最危急的关头抽身撤走——这一切情况使得一支即使在人数上和军事素质上都颇为可观的帝国军队，也完全产生不出与它相称的作用。

en: If the warlike weakness of Germany is neither a consequence of cowardice nor of military unfitness and of unfamiliarity with those skills which in modern times must not be lacking to bravery for victory, and on every occasion the imperial contingents give the greatest proofs of their courage and military self-sacrifice and prove themselves worthy of the old warlike fame of the Germans and their ancestors, then it is the arrangement of the whole and the general dissolution which let the exertions and sacrifices of individual men and corps go fruitlessly lost and lay upon them a curse that, however well they may strive, ruins all effect and consequence and puts them on a par with a farmer who wanted to sow the sea or plough up the rock.
zh: 如果说德意志在战争上的软弱，既不是胆怯的结果，也不是军事上的无能，不是对近代勇武求胜所不可缺的那些本领的陌生，而且一有机会，帝国各兵力就拿出勇气和军人牺牲精神的最大证据，证明自己配得上德意志人及其祖先昔日的战功，那么问题就出在整体的安排和普遍的涣散上：它们使单个人和单支队伍的投入与牺牲白白落空，并在上面压下一重诅咒，使他们无论怎样尽力，一切作用和后果都归于毁坏，把他们比作一个想往海里播种、想耕开岩石的农夫。

en: In the same case in which the German state power finds itself with regard to the war power, it finds itself with regard to the finances, which, after the European states have more or less departed from the feudal constitution, have become an essential part of that power which must lie immediately in the hands of the supreme state power.
zh: 德意志国家权力在军事力量上处于什么状况，在财政上也就处于同样的状况：自从欧洲各国或多或少脱离了封建采邑制之后，财政已经成为那种必须直接掌握在最高国家权力手里的权力之中本质的一部分。

en: To that extreme of financial organization according to which every expenditure that a public office, down to the commonest village judge, bailiff and further down, or any public need confined to a village, requires, as well as every kind of revenue as a contribution first flows up to the supreme state power and as state expenditure flows back down again into the smallest branches of public activity, through all the intermediate links of laws, decrees, accounts and officials, of which no collegium is in anything a highest resort — to this extreme the German lack of finances forms the other.
zh: 财政制度有这样一个极端：任何一笔支出——无论是直到最普通的村法官、捕役乃至更下面的差事，还是任何一种只限于一个村庄的公共需要所要求的支出——以及任何一种收入，都要作为摊款先向上流到最高国家权力那里，再作为国家支出，经过法律、法令、账目和官吏这一切中间环节，向下流回公共事务最细小的枝杈，而这些环节中没有一个机构在任何事情上是最高主管——与这个极端相对的另一极端，就是德意志的没有财政。

en: The great state objects and problems concerning the most just and least costly kind of contributions, state debts, state credit, which presses no estate before another — these and other things, which in other states require the expenditure of the greatest talents and in which mistakes have the most terrible consequences — these cares do not plague Germany.

There is on the whole neither the superfluous meddling of the state in every public cost — rather a village, a city, the guild of a city and so on attends itself to the financial matters that concern only it, under the general oversight but not under the commands of the state — nor, however, does a financial organization that would concern the state power itself take place.
zh: 赋税、国债、国家信用怎样才能最公正、花费最少、不使任何一个等级比另一个等级更受压迫，这些重大的国家事务和难题，以及其他种种在别的国家要耗掉最杰出人才的精力、一旦出错后果最为可怕的事情，这些操心并不折磨德意志。
总的说来，这里既没有国家对每一项公共开支的多余插手——一个村庄、一座城市、一座城市的行会等等，自己料理只与它们有关的那些财务，处在总的监督之下，却不受国家的命令——也没有一种会触及国家权力本身的财政制度。

en: The ordinary finances of Germany are in fact confined solely to the chamber taxes, which are paid by the estates for the maintenance of the chamber court.
They are accordingly very simple, and no Pitt is required to direct them.
zh: 德意志的常规财政其实只限于法院税这一项，也就是各等级为了维持帝国枢密法院而缴纳的税款。
因此它们非常简单，用不着一位皮特式的人物来主持。

en: The regular costs of the other supreme imperial court are in any case borne by the Emperor.
In more recent times a beginning has been made of founding a fund for this through the auctioning of imperial fiefs that have fallen back to the Empire.
zh: 另一个帝国最高法院的日常费用，反正本来就由皇帝承担。
近代已经开了头：通过拍卖重新归帝国所有的帝国封地，为此设立一笔基金。

en: Even on account of that single financial arrangement, the chamber dues, frequent complaints arise that they are badly paid, and remarkable as characterizing the German constitution is the reason for which Brandenburg does not pay the increase of them that was resolved several years ago: namely because it is doubtful whether in such things as general contributions to the state needs the majority of votes is binding for the individual.
Where this is doubtful, there is lacking that which alone constitutes a state: its unity in relation to the state power.
zh: 就连那唯一一项财政制度，也就是法院摊款，也常常有人抱怨说它们缴纳得很差；而勃兰登堡不肯缴纳几年前议决的那项加征，其理由最能说明德意志的宪法：因为它怀疑，在诸如向国家需要缴纳的普遍摊款这类事情上，多数票对单个成员究竟有没有约束力。
凡这一点可疑的地方，就缺少唯其才构成一个国家的东西：国家在国家权力方面的统一。

en: According to the principle of the feudal constitution, the contingents are paid by the estates themselves and provided with everything necessary.

It has already been recalled above that the urgent need in the last war induced several estates to give up the exercise of the right of the last point and to take the advantageous way out of a private agreement concerning joint provisioning with the imperial head, just as also smaller estates this time made no use of their right themselves to put their soldiers in the field and came to terms with larger estates that these should see to the furnishing of the contingent incumbent on the smaller estates.

One sees that — if herein lay a dawn of a transformation of the furnishing of the contingents, which is to be attended to by the estates, and of the delivery of their needs into money contributions to the common centre, which then takes over and arranges what is to be performed, and the beginning of a transition of the isolated and in a certain way personal performances into a genuine state institution with respect to war and financial organization, and of the transfer of the latter to the head, whereby the concept of a state alone realizes itself — this whole relation has partly affected only insignificant estates, partly has been a matter of passing accident.
zh: 按照封建采邑制的原则，各份兵力由各等级自己出钱，并由它们置办一切必需之物。
前面已经提过：上一场战争中的迫切需要，使好几个等级放弃行使最后一点的权利，转而采取一条有利的出路，即就共同给养与帝国元首订立私下协议；同样，较小的等级这一次也没有行使自己把士兵开赴战场的权利，而是与较大的等级谈妥，由后者负责派出本来应当由较小等级承担的那份兵力。
可以看出，如果说这里透出一线曙光，预示着由各等级操办的出兵和给养将变成向共同中心缴纳的货币摊款——这个中心届时接过应办之事并加以安排——，也预示着分散的、某种意义上属于个人的给付将过渡为真正的国家制度，在战争和财政方面都是如此，并把后者交给元首，而唯有通过这一点，国家的概念才得以实现，那么这整个关系一方面只涉及无关紧要的等级，另一方面也只是转瞬即逝的偶然。

en: As for the costs which, for those sides of a modern war that are not satisfied by the furnishing of soldiers, are to be contributed under the name of Roman months, the matter stands just the same as with the furnishing of the contingents.
According to the accounts of these, of the German Empire's war-operations treasury moneys, it has turned out that about half of what was resolved came in.

In the last months of the war before the opening of the Congress of Rastatt the public announcements of the cash balances in coin [gave] the whole sums of 300, 400 gulden; and while in other states the balance of the supreme war treasury, especially when it should be so small, is just not publicly made known, this announcement in the German Empire has no further influence on the enemy's war and peace operations against the imperial operations.
zh: 至于现代战争中有一些方面不是靠派出士兵就能应付的，为着这些方面，要按「罗马月」这个名目凑集一笔钱，这件事的情形与派出各份兵力完全一样。
从这些账目、即德意志帝国的战争行动金库款项的账目来看，已经表明：所议决的款项大约只收到了一半。
在拉施塔特会议开幕之前的战争最后几个月里，关于金库现金余额的公开通告[报出]的整数是 300、400 古尔登；而在别的国家，最高战事金库的余额，尤其在它小到这个地步时，恰恰是不会公开通告的，所以在德意志帝国，这种通告对敌人针对帝国军事行动的作战与媾和行动再也没有什么影响。

en: The principles that prevail in this matter — that the resolutions of the majority have no binding force for the minority, and that, on account of other connections, one cannot enter into the levying of Roman months resolved by the majority — are the same principles that hold with regard to the duties of the estates concerning military power.
zh: 这里通行的那些原则——多数派的决议对少数派没有约束力，由于另有别的联系，人们不能参与多数派所议决的罗马月捐的摊派——也就是那些在军力方面就等级义务而言有效的原则。

en: If formerly, with regard to finances, there was a kind of state power in the imperial tolls, the contributions of the imperial cities and the like, those times were nevertheless so utterly remote from the idea of a state and the concept of a universal that these revenues were regarded as the complete private property of the emperor, and the emperor could sell the revenues — which, however, is quite incomprehensible — and the estates could buy them or make them into a pledge that was subsequently rendered irredeemable, just as immediate state power too was bought or taken as a pledge, over which no stronger trait of barbarism in a people that forms a state can be hunted up.
zh: 如果说从前在财政方面，帝国的关税、帝国城市的捐输之类里面还有一种国家权力，那么那些时代毕竟离一个国家的观念和某种普遍之物的概念如此彻底地遥远，以致这些收入被看作皇帝的完全私有财产，皇帝可以卖掉这些收入——这一点却完全不可理解——而各等级可以买下它们，或把它们变成后来被弄成不可赎回的抵押品，正如直接的国家权力也曾被买下或用作抵押一样；在一个组成国家的民族那里，再也找不出比这更强烈的野蛮痕迹了。

en: It cannot be denied, however, that the need to create finances for Germany has from time to time been felt, and that proposals have been made to establish sources of money for the empire as a state.

Because at the same time the estates could not be minded to bring about this money-power through laws of contribution, since in that way something similar to the arrangement as it is in a state would have come about, both would have to be combined: to find a lasting fund for the state and neither to burden the estates nor in any manner or way to bind them.

Because the circumstance that the estates would be neither burdened nor bound was the most striking one, so that the whole thing was less a matter of seriousness than a pious wish — with which kind of wishes the true, inwardly lying indifference toward the object to which the wish applies, and at least the firm resolve to let it cost oneself nothing, is usually hidden behind a quite especially patriotic manner and mien —, so there is no doubt that, if the empire were just then occupied with a financial arrangement, in a company of honest imperial citizens the man who, for the best of the German empire, put forward the wish that a gold-mountain should grow up in Germany and that every ducat coined from it and, on first being issued, not used for the empire, should immediately run away like water, — [that] such a wisher would be regarded as the greatest German patriot who ever existed, because in the first moment they would have the feeling of not having to pay anything in such a way, before the reflection that through such a wish not a penny comes into the imperial treasury and, if the reflection really set in, they could still find expressed in it nothing other than what they themselves, despite their words, wanted.
zh: 然而不能否认，为德意志创造财政的需要不时被感受到，也有人提出过建议，要为作为国家的帝国开辟财源。
由于同时各等级不可能有意通过分摊的法律来造成这种金钱权力，因为那样就会产生某种类似于一个国家里那种安排的东西，所以两者必须结合起来：为国家找到一个持久的基金，同时既不加重各等级的负担，也不以任何方式约束它们。

因为各等级既不被加重负担也不被约束这一点最为突出，所以整件事与其说是认真的，不如说是一个虔诚的愿望——这类愿望通常把对愿望所指向之事的真正内在的漠不关心，以及至少那种决不肯让自己花一个钱的坚定决心，藏在一副装得特别爱国的姿态和神情后面——，因此无可怀疑：如果帝国恰好正在着手一项财政安排，那么在一群诚实的帝国公民当中，有谁为了德意志帝国的利益提出这样的愿望，说德意志该长出一座金山，从那里铸出的每一个杜卡特，第一次发行时若没有用在帝国身上，就该立刻像水一样流走，——〔那么〕提出这种愿望的人就会被看作有史以来最伟大的德意志爱国者，因为他们在最初一刻先有的是那种这样就不必掏钱的感觉，而后才会想到：靠这样一个愿望，帝国金库里不会多出一个芬尼，而即使他们现实地想起来，他们也还是会发现，这话里说出来的无非是他们自己不顾嘴上所说而真正想要的东西。

en: Apart from this, older imperial diets designated for the need of such a fund not such ideal, merely imagined sources, but — without any estate having to sacrifice anything of what is its own — really existing lands, actual realities, for defraying the expenses of imperial affairs, just as those hunters [designated] a real, not an imagined bear for the payment of their reckoning.
zh: 撇开这一点不谈，早先的帝国议会为着这样一种基金的需要，指定的并不是那种观念的、纯属想象出来的来源，而是——同时任何一个等级都不必牺牲自己所有物中的任何东西——现实地存在着的土地，地地道道的实在之物，用来支付帝国事务的开销，就像那些猎人用一头真实的、并非想象出来的熊来付他们的账一样。

en: Several hundred years ago a law was made, that for the establishment of an imperial fund all those lands should be designated which have fallen into the hands of foreign nations, if the German empire brings them back to itself; and in the wars themselves, in which the opportunity was thus present for the German empire to bring them back to itself, it has always known how to arrange matters so that it lost still more, and thus enlarged the imperial fund.
Thus the loss of the left bank of the Rhine, too, must be viewed from a more consoling side, namely as a way of the possibility of founding an imperial financial fund.
zh: 几百年前有过一条法律，规定为了设立帝国基金，凡是落入外国民族手中的土地，一旦德意志帝国把它们重新收归自己，就都应当被指定为此用；而在那些战争本身当中，既然存在着德意志帝国把它们重新收归自己的机会，它却总是懂得把事情安排成自己失去得更多，也就是把帝国基金扩大了。
因此，莱茵河左岸的丧失也必须从一个更令人安慰的方面来看，即看作有可能设立帝国财政基金的一条途径。

en: If such thoughts, thorough in their time — and one can be sure that, if even now a German teacher of constitutional law were spoken to about the unhappy lack of finances, he would vindicate the perfection of this side of the German imperial constitution as well by the path pointed out — were still capable of it, that the German character, sanguine in such hopes, could place a hope on them in the present political condition of Europe and Germany, yet they cannot be reckoned with when we consider whether Germany possesses the kind of power that in our times belongs to the essence of a state, a money-power in deed and at the present time in which we are speaking.
zh: 如果这类在当时是彻底的念头——人们可以肯定，如果现在还有人向一位德意志的国家法教师谈起财政上这种不幸的匮乏，他也会用所指出的这条途径来为德意志帝国宪法这一方面的完善性作辩护——还有能力让那种在此类希望中抱乐观态度的德意志性格，在当下欧洲和德意志的政治状况下对它们抱一种希望，那么在考虑到德意志是否拥有在我们时代属于一个国家之本质的那种权力、即在事实上并且在我们此刻说话的当下是否拥有一种金钱权力时，它们还是不能被计算在内。

en: Formerly there was a particular way, when — not in a foreign war, but in one against a rebellious and outlawed estate — one estate had costs for the state, of bearing this general expense and compensating the latter.

For if executions of declarations of outlawry and other decisions of the imperial courts, which is not always the case, were really set in motion, the costs fell to the charge of the losing party, namely if it is defeated not merely in law but also in war.
The imperial execution army of the Seven Years' War received no compensation for its trouble.

That way of getting the execution costs paid was, in older times, a mighty spur sometimes really to execute a declaration of outlawry, in that the executing party kept the lands of the executed party without further right and without any closer reckoning otherwise, — as the Swiss came into possession of the greater part of the old Habsburg ancestral possessions, Bavaria into possession of Donauwörth, etc.
zh: 从前有一种特别的做法：当——不是在一场对外战争中，而是在一场针对某个叛乱并被处以帝国禁令的等级的战争中——一个等级为国家承担了费用时，就由大家来承担这项普遍开销，并补偿后者。
因为如果对帝国禁令宣告和其他帝国法院裁定的执行——这并不总是实情——现实地被启动起来，那么费用就落在败诉一方的身上，也就是说，如果它不只是在法律上败诉，而且在战争中也败了的话。
七年战争的帝国执行军为它的辛劳没有得到任何赔偿。
那种让执行费用得到偿付的做法，在较早的时代是一根强有力的马刺，促使人们有时现实地去执行一项帝国禁令，因为执行的一方不必有任何进一步的权利，也不必作任何更细致的清算，就保住了被执行的等级的土地，——就像瑞士人取得旧日哈布斯堡祖传领地的大部分、巴伐利亚取得多瑙沃特等等那样。

en: A multitude that has not known how to form any state power through this dissolution of military power and lack of finances is unable to defend its [sc. the people's] independence against foreign enemies.

It must necessarily see it go to ruin, if not all at once, then gradually, must in war be exposed to all plundering and devastation, must necessarily bear the main costs of the same for friend and foe, must lose provinces to foreign powers and, with state power over the individual members annihilated and overlordship over the vassals lost, must contain within itself nothing but sovereign states, which as such behave toward one another according to power and cunning, whose stronger ones spread out and whose weaker ones are devoured, and which, the more significant ones, are nevertheless again powerless against a great power.
zh: 一群由于这种军力的解体以及财政的匮乏而未能形成任何国家权力的人，无力抵御外敌以保卫它〔即人民〕的独立。
它必然会眼看着这群人——即使不是一下子，也是逐渐地——走向毁灭，在战争中必然遭到一切劫掠和破坏，必然为友为敌承担战争的主要费用，必然把一些省份丢给外部势力，而在对各单个成员的国家权力已被消灭、对封臣的宗主权力也已丧失的情况下，它自身所包含的就无非是一些主权国家；这些国家作为主权国家彼此依凭实力和狡计相待，其中较强的不停扩张，较弱的被吞掉，而那些比较重要的国家面对一个大国时又仍然无能为力。
